pack.description: Vocabulary of history passages and talks: states, power, sources and social change.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory history texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: a series of rulers who all belong to the same family
entries.example_academic: The dynasty ruled for three centuries before a succession dispute divided the court.
entries.example_spoken: That vase is from the Ming dynasty.

entries.definition: relating to a country that controls and governs another land, or to the period of that control
entries.example_academic: Colonial administrators redrew boundaries with little regard for existing communities.
entries.example_spoken: The old town still has a lot of colonial architecture.

entries.definition: a formal written agreement between two or more countries
entries.example_academic: The treaty ended the war but left the border question unresolved.
entries.example_spoken: They signed a treaty to share the river's water.

entries.definition: the period during which a king, queen or emperor rules
entries.example_academic: During her reign, the kingdom doubled its territory.
entries.example_spoken: The palace was built in the reign of Louis the Fourteenth.

entries.definition: the act of taking control of a land or people by force
entries.example_academic: The conquest of the valley gave the empire access to its silver mines.
entries.example_spoken: The course starts with the Norman conquest.

entries.definition: relating to the period of European history between about the years 500 and 1500
entries.example_academic: Medieval towns were governed by councils of wealthy merchants.
entries.example_spoken: We visited a medieval castle on the field trip.

entries.definition: a system of government in which a king or queen is the head of state
entries.example_academic: The monarchy survived the revolution only by surrendering most of its powers.
entries.example_spoken: Spain is still a monarchy, isn't it?

entries.definition: a collection of historical documents and records, or the place where they are kept
entries.example_academic: The letters lay unread in a provincial archive for two hundred years.
entries.example_spoken: I spent the summer working in the university archive.

entries.definition: a written record of events in the order in which they happened
entries.example_academic: The chronicle describes the famine in detail but never mentions its causes.
entries.example_spoken: The book is a chronicle of one family over a century.

entries.definition: a person who takes a job or position after someone else
entries.example_academic: His successor reversed most of the reforms within a year.
entries.example_spoken: They still haven't named a successor for the department head.

entries.definition: to officially end a law, system or institution
entries.example_academic: Parliament abolished the tax after months of rural protest.
entries.example_spoken: They should abolish attendance grades, honestly.

entries.definition: an occasion when a large group of people fight against those who rule them
entries.example_academic: The uprising began in the ports and spread inland within weeks.
entries.example_spoken: The film is about a student uprising in the sixties.

entries.definition: relating to the medieval system in which people received land and protection in return for work and military service
entries.example_academic: Feudal obligations tied peasants to the estate on which they were born.
entries.example_spoken: It's a very feudal way of running a company.

entries.definition: the traditions, buildings and culture that a society receives from the past and values
entries.example_academic: The dispute concerned who should control the nation's archaeological heritage.
entries.example_spoken: The old station is protected as part of the city's heritage.

entries.definition: a person who held a job or position before someone else
entries.example_academic: Unlike his predecessor, the new governor negotiated with local leaders.
entries.example_spoken: My predecessor left the files in a complete mess.

entries.definition: the class of people with the highest social rank, often with land and titles passed down in families
entries.example_academic: The aristocracy resisted any reform that threatened its exemption from taxation.
entries.example_spoken: The novel makes fun of the English aristocracy.

entries.definition: the study of how history has been written, or the body of historical writing on a subject
entries.example_academic: Recent historiography has shifted attention from rulers to ordinary households.
entries.example_spoken: The first chapter of my thesis is just historiography.

entries.definition: the ancient past, especially the period of the Greek and Roman civilizations
entries.example_academic: Few texts from antiquity survive in anything close to their original form.
entries.example_spoken: That road has been used since antiquity.

entries.definition: the complete power of a country to govern itself
entries.example_academic: The treaty recognized the sovereignty of the new republic.
entries.example_spoken: The debate was about sovereignty, not about trade.

entries.definition: to take control of a territory next to your own, usually by force
entries.example_academic: The kingdom annexed the coastal provinces without a formal declaration of war.
entries.example_spoken: The city annexed two suburbs in the fifties.

entries.definition: to give up the position of king or queen, or to refuse to accept a responsibility
entries.example_academic: The king abdicated in favor of his son after the military defeat.
entries.example_spoken: You can't just abdicate responsibility for the group project.

entries.definition: a division of a group, especially a religious one, into two opposing parts because of a disagreement
entries.example_academic: The schism divided the church along linguistic as well as doctrinal lines.
entries.example_spoken: There's a real schism in the department over the new curriculum.

entries.definition: the right to vote in political elections
entries.example_academic: Universal suffrage was achieved only after decades of organized protest.
entries.example_spoken: Women's suffrage came surprisingly late in some countries.

entries.definition: the act of freeing a person or group from legal, social or political control
entries.example_academic: Emancipation did not immediately bring economic independence to former slaves.
entries.example_spoken: The lecture covered the emancipation of serfs in Russia.

entries.definition: in the Middle Ages, a person who promised loyalty and service to a lord in return for land; a state controlled by another
entries.example_academic: Each vassal owed his lord forty days of military service a year.
entries.example_spoken: The smaller kingdom was basically a vassal of the empire.

entries.definition: the old economic theory that a country grows rich by selling more goods abroad than it buys
entries.example_academic: Under mercantilism, colonies existed to supply raw materials to the home country.
entries.example_spoken: Mercantilism explains why they taxed foreign cloth so heavily.

entries.definition: a violent attempt by a group of people to take control of their country from the government
entries.example_academic: The insurrection was suppressed, but its demands shaped later legislation.
entries.example_spoken: The newspapers called it an insurrection, not a protest.

entries.definition: to officially leave a country or organization and become independent
entries.example_academic: Three provinces threatened to secede unless the tax was withdrawn.
entries.example_spoken: What happens if a region votes to secede?

entries.definition: a document or object created at the time being studied, by someone who was there
entries.example_academic: Historians treat a diary as a primary source but must still question its author's motives.
entries.example_spoken: You need at least three primary sources for the paper.
